Subject: POC trial environment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for your time earlier today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and ownership.

Summary (from today's discovery):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for real-time recommendation use case in Acme's web app (latency target 200ms p95).
- Data: sample query/response logs and a 10k-row test dataset.
- Success criteria: p95 latency <= 200ms for 1-2k RPS peak, embedding similarity >= 0.82 on internal eval set, and cost estimate within agreed threshold.

Environment options we discussed:
1) Hosted sandbox (fastest to start) — Redwood-managed, short-lived keys, good for functional validation and throughput rough estimates.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput, for high-concurrency stress tests; requires capacity reservation.
3) VPC/private deployment (hosted VPC or on-prem) — for security/compliance and network-lockdown testing; longer setup and procurement.

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Technical kickoff (30–45m) to review runbook and finalize required artifacts (sample data, network allowlists, security contacts): Connor to lead — target Thu 20 Aug.
- Hosted sandbox prep: Connor to provision a hosted sandbox with example model/quantization profile and shared API key.
- Success criteria & evaluation plan: Monica to own metrics collection and run eval script; Priyom to help draft acceptance tests for model quality and cost.
- Procurement/terms: Marissa to loop in Jenna for any contract/procurement timeline needs.

Please reply with any corrections, availability for the 20th (preferred windows: 9–11am PT or 2–4pm PT), and whether you want us to start with hosted sandbox or go straight to a VPC trial.

Attachments: initial POC runbook (v1) attached.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical notes and a recommended path:

Recommendation: start with hosted sandbox for functional validation and latency profiling; move to dedicated sandbox for throughput/stress tests; only do VPC if there are strict allowlist or data residency requirements that can't be met by hosted VPC offering. This minimizes time-to-insight.

Hosted sandbox details (what I'll provision):
- Short-lived API key scoped to a test project.
- Model variant: rwd-rlhf-3b quantized (good balance for latency and quality).
- Default batching/kv-cache settings tuned for low-latency; will send sample config.
- Test harness endpoints + a small load script we can run from your infra to emulate 1k RPS (we'll provide a Docker container).

Dedicated sandbox notes:
- Minimum reservation: 1 month for our dedicated sandbox offering (can do prorated adjustments for POC if we agree).
- Estimated cost: we'll provide a rough cost table during kickoff; ballpark figures will be included in the runbook.

VPC items:
- Hosted VPC (our recommended VPC trial) is faster than on-prem and supports customer-managed subnets + allowlist. Expected setup time: 5–10 business days pending network approvals.

Timeline suggestion:
- Thu 20 Aug: technical kickoff (Connor leads) — finalize artifacts and start hosted sandbox (1–2 business days to provision).
- Mon 24 Aug: smoke tests + initial latency report.
- Week of 31 Aug: throughput/stress tests (if we move to dedicated sandbox).

Action items assigned:
- Connor: provision hosted sandbox, share API key and test harness, draft config snippets.
- Monica: finalize success metric definitions and provide eval script (will validate embedding threshold and p95 calculation).
- Priyom: help define acceptance tests and cost measurement plan.
- Marissa: own procurement contact and contracting questions; coordinate DocuSign if needed.

I attached the POC runbook (v1) and a link to the shared Drive folder with test artifacts.
